 From revised PNB credit card fees and inactive bank account rules to life certificate submission and the extended ITR deadline, here's what customers, pensioners and taxpayers need to know.
 Here are four important financial and banking updates in November. | Representational image/AI generated.
 November brings important updates for bank customers, pensioners, and taxpayers. Punjab National Bank (PNB) is revising credit card charges, certain inactive accounts may require reactivation, pensioners must submit life certificates, and eligible taxpayers have a revised ITR deadline.

 PNB charges to pension rules: Here are four important financial and banking updates in November 
 1. Pensioners must submit Life Certificates
 Pensioners below 80 must submit their annual life certificate, also known as Jeevan Pramaan Patra , between November 1 and November 30. The certificate confirms their eligibility to receive pension payments. Failure to submit it within the prescribed period could disrupt pension payments. Eligible pensioners can use digital submission facilities. 
 2. ITR filing deadline
 The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has extended the income tax return filing deadline for specified audit cases for FY 2025-26 from October 31 to November 21, 2026. The extension does not cover every taxpayer, so eligible businesses should verify the applicable requirements. 
 3. PNB credit card charges
 PNB will introduce revised credit card service charges from November 1, 2026. Reward redemption will cost ₹99 per request, while utility bill payments exceeding ₹50,000 in a billing cycle will attract a 1% fee, capped at ₹2,000 per transaction. Cash withdrawal charges and late payment fees will also change. Applicable GST will be extra, and charges may vary by card variant.
 4. PNB inactive accounts
 Customers with certain PNB accounts that have maintained a zero balance and recorded no customer-initiated transactions for over three years may need to complete KYC formalities by November 10, 2026 , to avoid closure. Customers should contact their branches to confirm whether their accounts fall under the specified category.
